text:
Tyson Foerster played only 29 games last season, and The Hockey News put it well this month: he is finding his game. Nine points in his last ten, two goals in his last three, including a snipe on the power play against Vancouver on Friday that Charlie O'Connor of PHLY Sports called mostly about Foerster and his shot. That shot is the calling card, clocked in the 95th percentile.

Fourteen points in 27 games, six on the power play, at 17 minutes a night. His own finishing is right on the number, six goals on 6.0 expected. The luck is in the assists: Philadelphia has scored 7.1 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, so some of the recent point surge rides on teammates shooting hot.

The harder number is at five on five. The Flyers have only 44% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there, about the same as without him, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had his line leaning on dump-ins last season. With 50 hits he plays the heavy game. Watch whether more of those shifts end in the offensive zone.
